claim: Five boards draw page folders — 'Marketing 3', 'Legal 2' — as a first-class part of the site's page structure, and the captions treat them as a nesting rule ('Folders nest one level only', 'Counts survive the collapse').
truth: Folders exist only in one browser's localStorage. They are not in ProjectData, never reach the server, are invisible to a teammate, are gone on a second device, and are destroyed by clearing site data. The engine has no folder concept at all.
evidence: useFolders.ts:24 `const STORAGE_KEY_PREFIX = 'pg-folders-v1-'`; :33-52 `load()` reads `localStorage.getItem(storageKey(siteId))`; :55-62 `persist()` writes the same key and swallows quota errors. The module docstring :3-4 states it outright: 'Folders are a UI organisational concept, NOT stored in the engine.' FolderItem is declared in pages/types.ts:15-20 and appears nowhere in ProjectData (shared/types/project.ts:30-48, whose fields are version/pages/pagesOrder/styles/assets/metadata/settings/dsSchemaVersion/cmsBindings). PagesTab.tsx:57 scopes the store by `getSiteIdFromUrl()`. Prior finding MOD-B-09.

Append to 155:19: 'The counts are local too.' Do NOT delete the folder rows — the feature works, it just does not travel. claim: The board's own annotation reads: 'role="alert" aria-live="assertive" · .bd-pg-name-error, 11px --bk-error. The commit is refused; the row stays in edit.'
truth: Every clause is true except the last one's implication. The row does stay in edit — and the user can never leave it with a corrected name. PageRow latches a one-shot `committedRef` on the first commit attempt, and nothing resets it while the row is still renaming, so a second Enter and the blur both return early. The only exit is Escape, which throws the edit away. The board draws a recoverable validation error over a dead end.
evidence: PageRow.tsx:74 `const committedRef = React.useRef(false)`; :87-91 `commitOnce` returns immediately when `committedRef.current` is true and sets it before calling `onRenameCommit`; :76-85 the effect that clears it runs only on `[isRenaming, page.name]`, and the refusal changes NEITHER (PagesTab.tsx:99-108 sets `nameError` and returns without calling `p.commitRename`, so `renamingPageId` and `page.name` are unchanged). Enter (:94-96) and blur (:265) both route through `commitOnce`. Escape (:97-101) sets `committedRef.current = true` and cancels.
edit: Amend 1717:17234's last sentence to: 'The commit is refused and the row stays in edit — but the rename cannot be re-committed (PageRow.tsx:74/87-91 latch after the first attempt); Escape is the only exit and it discards the edit.' Keep the alert styling note as-is; it matches PageRow.tsx:269-273 exactly.

claim: 'RENAMING (F2) · EMPTY · TOO SHORT · VALID' — three validation states, and every one of them matches the shipped tab-bar rename exactly.
truth: The three states are right. What the spec sheet does not say is that this rename and the sidebar rename obey different rules: the tab bar refuses an empty name and warns under three characters but never checks for a duplicate, while the sidebar refuses duplicates (board 1717:17217) and has no length rule at all. Two rename surfaces, two rulebooks, and each board draws only its own half.
evidence: PageTabBar.tsx:66-74 `validateName` — `if (!trimmed) return { error: 'Page name is required', slug: '' }; if (trimmed.length < 3) return { warning: 'Short name — consider 3+ characters', slug };` — no duplicate check; :286 Enter is gated on `!nameValidation.error` only. PagesTab.tsx:99-105 the sidebar path: `p.pages.some((pg) => pg.id !== pageId && pg.name.toLowerCase() === trimmed.toLowerCase())` -> `setNameError('A page with this name already exists')` — no length check; PageRow.tsx:96 commits `renameValue.trim() || page.name` so an empty name silently reverts instead of erroring.

claim: The page rows carry a ⌂ glyph on Home and no status chip on any row — no Live, no Draft, no Hidden badge anywhere in the family.
truth: The boards are right and a prior reading of the code was not. The panel renders NO status chip and no home chip: `getStatusLabel` is computed and spent entirely on the row's aria-label. Seven `.bd-pg-chip` colour variants sit in the stylesheet with no consumer, and two tests assert the chips are absent. So MOD-B-16's 'the panel badge says Draft on a page the exporter ships live' is a screen-reader-only disagreement, not a visible one — the harm is real but smaller than filed, and no board is wrong.
evidence: PageRow.tsx:139 `const label = getStatusLabel(page.status ?? 'live')`; :141-149 `label` is used only inside `ariaLabel`; the render (:160-318) contains no chip element. PagesTab.css:296-302 defines `.bd-pg-chip.live/.draft/.scheduled/.hidden/.password/.external/.error` — grep across packages/editor/src for `bd-pg-chip` / `bd-pg-home-chip` returns only the CSS and two negative assertions: PageRow.test.tsx:65-73 ('no home/status chips on the tree row; status still announced') and PagesTab.test.tsx:194-200 ('scheduled status is announced, not chipped (board 140:2 rows carry no chips)'). The ⌂ the boards draw is the icon slot itself, PageRow.tsx:231-255.
edit: No edit. Recording it so the chip vocabulary is not re-added to these boards from MOD-B-16 or MOD-B-27; the four unwritable PageStatus members (scheduled / error / external / draft-as-a-value) have no producer and should not gain one in Figma either.

claim: Nothing in the 25-board Pages section draws a generated, dynamic or CMS-backed route, and caption 155:24 explicitly retires the reading that once did: '(The card board described CMS-generated pages here; cargo-sheets §2 defines Listings as the SEO table.)'
truth: That retirement is correct, and MOD-A-09's measurement supports it: nothing in packages/editor calls cms.dynamicPages and the Pages panel has zero CMS references. So there is no mark-unimplemented to file on this axis. The gap runs the OTHER way — the product does generate dynamic pages at publish and the Pages panel cannot list them — but that is a missing capability, not a lying board, and drawing it would be inventing design rather than recording it.
evidence: Board text read across all 25 boards in 1776:8377: no occurrence of 'blog', 'collection', 'dynamic', 'generated' or a ':slug' route. The panel's list is built solely from `composer.elements.getAllPages()` (usePages.ts:103) with no server call. Publish-side generation is cms.service.ts:226-241 `appendDynamicPagesToPublish`, which matches `pages.find((p) => p.path === col.pageTemplatePath)` against an EXPORT FILENAME from ExportEngine.buildPageHrefs (:787-796) — so a slug change unbinds it silently (MOD-B-21). Content's own 'Dynamic pages' screen is W-C-28's missing board, in section 06.
edit: No edit in this section. If the coordinator wants the capability surfaced, it belongs on the Content side (W-C-28) first; a Pages-tree group for generated pages would be a design proposal, not a truth correction, and this pass does not make those.

claim: The Pages tree is drawn flat: folders at one level, pages inside them or at the root, and no page nested under another page. Caption 155:18 asserts 'Folders nest one level only.'
truth: Correct. `PageData` has no parent field of any kind — the whole record is id / name / slug / isHome / root / styles / settings / meta / updatedAt / slugManuallySet / slugHistory — and `FolderItem` holds a flat `pageIds` array with no parent, so a folder cannot contain a folder. The one place hierarchy appears anywhere in the product is the Structure view, which derives it from '/' segments in slugs and stores nothing (FIG-B-17).
evidence: shared/types/project.ts:144-176 PageData in full — no parentId, no children, no path. pages/types.ts:15-20 `FolderItem { id; name; pageIds: string[]; collapsed: boolean }`. PageFolder.tsx renders `pages.map(<PageRow nested/>)` and never recurses into another PageFolder. PageManager.ts has no parent-aware verb: createPage :61, updatePage :116 (name/slug/settings/slugManuallySet/meta only), setActivePage :222, setHomePage :239, deletePage :254, duplicatePage :293, reorderPage :337, importPage :362.
edit: No edit. Recorded so 'depth-5 tree' language elsewhere in the file (the S1-stress board, 55:2, is named '40 pages · depth-5 tree') is not read back into this section as a page hierarchy — at most it is folders plus slug segments.

claim: No board in the section draws a drag-in-flight or drop-indicator state, and none draws the page-recovery state.
truth: Two different reasons, and only one is a Figma gap. Reorder IS implemented and IS reachable by mouse — every row is draggable and every row is a drop target — but the code renders no visible feedback for it either (W-F-14 filed exactly this), so the board and the product are equally blank and the fix is code-first. Page recovery is different: RecoveryManager replaces a page whose root has gone missing with an empty container and renders nothing at all, so there is no state for a board to be right or wrong about.
evidence: Reorder: PageRow.tsx:171-174 (`draggable`, `onDragStart`, `onDragOver`, `onDrop`), :110-127 the handlers, PageList.tsx:312-315 `onReorderDrop={(draggedId) => composer?.elements.reorderPage(draggedId, page.id)}`, PageManager.ts:337-356 rebuilds the Map and emits PROJECT_CHANGED{'page:reordered'}. The indicator element exists but nothing toggles it: PageList.tsx:351 `<div className='bd-pg-drop-indicator' aria-hidden='true' />` with the comment 'toggled via .show during dragover (CSS owns visibility)' and no code anywhere adds `.show`. Recovery: RecoveryManager.ts:168-197 emits EVENTS.PAGE_RECOVERED and nothing listens (MOD-B-02).
edit: No edit. Recorded to close the coverage question: 'reorder has no board' is true and already W-F-14's; 'recovery has no board' is true and is not actionable in Figma until the product draws something.
